transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 65 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Mateo Rivera (Redwood Solutions), Amira Khan (HelioSync CTO), Luca Moretti (HelioSync Head Cloud), Priya Desai (HelioSync Security), Owen Park (HelioSync PM)

Summary:
Quick technical sync focused on marketplace packaging requirements, on-prem/VPC listing constraints, and quantization/latency tradeoffs for HelioSync's inference gateway. Action items assigned; agreed pilot window and artifacts to exchange.

Topics covered:
- Marketplace listing packaging (Helm, manifests, billing SKU)
- KMS/HSM integration and audit logs
- Quantization strategy for mixed CPU/GPU footprint
- Autoscaling and canary routing for marketplace tenants
- Pilot plan: 24-hour latency + cost run on dev cluster

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Li: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood — I think we have the core folks from HelioSync here?
00:23 Amira Khan: Yep, hi Jordan, Amira here. Thanks. We wanted to get into the nitty gritty around listing — what you need from us and how the quantization tradeoffs look.
00:38 Jordan Li: Great, we'll kick off. Sofia's our SE, she'll walk through packaging and the quantization playbook. Mateo's on for ops notes.
01:05 Sofia Patel: Hi all. Quick note — we'll go through the packaging checklist first, then the quantization guidance, then time for infra specifics. Apologies in advance, audio from my end is a little windy.
01:35 Luca Moretti: No worries. Also to call out, our marketplace team is strict about the helm artifacts and image signing, and we also need a small footprint option for edge tenants.
02:10 Sofia Patel: Understood. For Redwood marketplace listings we typically require: Helm chart with templated values, OCI image references, a clear RBAC manifest, and a start-up probe for health checks. We also add a metadata YAML that includes supported regions, billing SKU, and resource footprint.
02:45 Owen Park: When you say "billing SKU" — is that something Redwood injects or we define?
03:02 Jordan Li: Good question. For partner listings the partner typically defines SKU mapping in their listing config; Redwood's marketplace connector maps usage-based metering to that SKU. We can share the sample manifest.
03:30 Amira Khan: Perfect. Also need to confirm networking — VPC peering vs private link. HelioSync prefers private link for our gov customers.
03:50 Sofia Patel: We support both. For VPC/private link we'll need the CIDR ranges and peering role. Important: if you use private link, audit logs and flow logs need to surface to your control plane — we add instrumentation hooks.
04:20 Priya Desai: On audit logs: we need to ensure the logs include per-request model variant, token counts, and cryptographic key ID where applicable. Is that feasible?
04:45 Mateo Rivera: Yes, we can emit request-level traces with model identifier, payload size, and token estimate. The token estimate may be off by a bit — transcription quality usually noisy.
05:10 Priya Desai: Ha, yes — but we need consistent key IDs for KMS mapping. Can Redwood accept a customer-managed KMS?
05:28 Sofia Patel: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) via KMS/HSM. For marketplace, if you're listing a private deployment we can hook into your KMS; for hosted listings partners typically use Redwood-managed keys unless there's an enterprise contract.
05:58 Luca Moretti: Good. For HelioSync we will likely need a hybrid: hosted control plane but customer-managed keys for specific tenants.
06:18 Jordan Li: That's a common pattern. We'll share the KMS integration doc. Expect to see requirements around key rotation windows, envelope encryption approach, and an API for retrieving key metadata.
06:45 Amira Khan: On quantization — our ML team wants to push 8-bit quant models to reduce cost. Does Redwood have guidance for that?
07:10 Sofia Patel: We do. High-level: 8-bit quantization (Q8) gives big memory and throughput wins on GPUs that support it, but you need to validate quality on your prompt sets. Also some kernels perform better in 16-bit for certain ops; we recommend A/B testing.
07:43 Luca Moretti: Any red flags for LLM kernels? We run models with long context windows and KV cache heavy workloads.
08:05 Sofia Patel: KV cache behavior matters — quantizing can change the numerical stability of attention and KV ops. Our runtime has a quant-safe execution path that uses mixed precision for KV cache to avoid regressions. But that path has a small perf delta. We'll provide specific perf numbers for collapsed sequences.
08:35 Mateo Rivera: Also watch compilation time and kernel selection: if we fallback to a non-optimised kernel because of quant mismatch, latency could spike. We'll include recommended quant configs per model family.
09:10 Owen Park: Could we get a sample benchmark showing tokens/sec and p95 latency between FP16 and Q8 for one of your verified models?
09:32 Jordan Li: Yes — action item: we'll send a benchmark spreadsheet with tokens/sec, p95, and cost per 1M tokens for FP16 vs Q8 on a T4-equivalent and an A10G-equivalent GPU.
09:54 Amira Khan: Great. On the marketplace packaging side, we also have a smaller edge SKU that runs partly on CPU. Any tips for quant+CPU?
10:20 Sofia Patel: CPU quantization can be useful but results are more variable. For CPU inference we often recommend int8 kernels and a smaller sequence length cap. We'll add a small break-down: CPU-optimized quant profiles vs GPU-optimized.
10:48 Priya Desai: Security question — SSO and RBAC for tenant onboarding. HelioSync wants SAML integration into our console plus LDAP for on-prem customers.
11:10 Jordan Li: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For RBAC we can import LDAP groups as role bindings during onboarding. For marketplace listings, we can surface SSO integration steps in the listing docs.
11:40 Luca Moretti: Does the marketplace require an operator/agent to run on customer infra?
11:55 Sofia Patel: We ship a small operator for on-prem connectors — it's optional for hosted deployments. The operator handles telemetry, image updates, and registry auth. It runs as a DaemonSet if you need node-level hooks.
12:20 Amira Khan: Ok, what about image signing — the marketplace prereq was signed images. Do you have sigstore or cosign integration?
12:35 Mateo Rivera: Yes, we prefer cosign signatures for OCI images. Partner checklist includes cosign sigs and a checksum in the metadata YAML.
12:55 Owen Park: Can you remind us about the canary routing options? We want to do gradual rollout across tenants.
13:18 Sofia Patel: We support per-tenant canaries, A/B traffic split at the gateway, and automatic fallback to a pinned compatible model variant if the canary passes latency/cost checks. You configure the rollout policy in the listing's routing policy section.
13:48 Priya Desai: Do those policies show up in audit logs?
14:05 Mateo Rivera: Yes — rollout events (start, percent, rollback) are recorded with timestamps and operator ID.
14:30 Luca Moretti: We're also curious about pricing: for marketplace listing, if we want a usage-based component plus a reserved capacity for enterprise, how does billing map?
14:50 Jordan Li: You can define multiple SKUs: e.g., sku.reserve, sku.usage. The marketplace connector maps usage metrics to the usage SKU; reserved capacity is a contract outside the marketplace but can be surfaced as a plan in the listing metadata. We'll share the SKU mapping doc.
15:20 Amira Khan: Can we do a short demo of how you instrument token-level cost breakdown?
15:45 Sofia Patel: Sure — quick screen share. [screen share begins, audio description: Sofia walks through Redwood Console token breakdown].
17:00 Sofia Patel: Here's a trace: token split per prompt, model variant, and kernel type — you can filter by tenant, route, or model.
17:30 Amira Khan: I love the ability to filter by kernel. Curious — how do you detect kernel fallbacks?
17:48 Mateo Rivera: We log kernel type used per request; fallback is flagged when selected kernel differs from the compiled preferred kernel for that model/sequence combo.
18:10 Luca Moretti: For our pilot we need a reproducible harness to send traffic. Does Redwood provide a load generator?
18:30 Jordan Li: We have a lightweight runner used for internal benchmarks — we'll package it for partners. It can replay prompts and measure tokens/sec and p95. We'll add it to the benchmark spreadsheet.
18:55 Priya Desai: On compliance — SOC2 scope and penetration testing frequency?
19:12 Jordan Li: Redwood is SOC2 Type II; we do pen tests quarterly and can share redacted reports under NDA. For marketplace listing we'll need to confirm the shared responsibility model in writing.
19:38 Amira Khan: Noted. For the pilot credentials, what's the recommended least-privilege role?
19:50 Sofia Patel: We ask for an API key scoped to a sandbox tenant with read/write limited to inference endpoints and telemetry, no billing permissions. For on-prem connector tests, a Kubernetes service account with limited RBAC is fine.
20:15 Luca Moretti: We'll provision that.
20:30 Owen Park: A quick note — HelioSync's model uses very long contexts (up to 60k tokens) for summarization. Any special guidance?
20:50 Sofia Patel: For 60k contexts the memory footprint is huge; recommended to use segmented KV caching and to pin a larger sequence-optimized kernel. Quantization helps but you must validate attention stability. We'll include recommended kernel flags for longcontext runs.
21:20 Amira Khan: Regarding deployment artifacts, can we host images in our registry?
21:35 Jordan Li: Yes, you can host images in your registry; the listing just points to the OCI ref. We also support pulling via partner registry credentials injected into the operator.
21:58 Priya Desai: One more security item — HSM-backed key usage for signing artifacts. Can you verify signature provenance in the listing flow?
22:20 Mateo Rivera: We can verify cosign signatures and record the signer key id in the listing metadata. HSM-based keys are supported if you can produce a public key for verification.
22:45 Luca Moretti: Great.
23:00 Jordan Li: Ok, quick recap before we assign action items — Sofia do you want to recap packaging needs?
23:12 Sofia Patel: Sure. Packaging checklist: Helm chart, templated values, OCI image with cosign signature, metadata YAML with SKU mapping, health/startup probes, RBAC manifests, operator (optional), and docs for SSO/SCIM. Also include a small edge/CPU profile and a default GPU profile.
23:45 Amira Khan: And quantization guidance?
23:50 Sofia Patel: We'll provide per-model-family recommended quant profiles (Q8 GB, mixed precision KV), a benchmark comparing FP16 vs Q8 on target GPUs, and a CPU int8 profile for edge. We'll also include known caveats for long-KV contexts.
24:15 Jordan Li: Pilot plan? HelioSync will provision dev cluster creds, Redwood will run a 24-hour benchmark runner and provide tokens/sec, p95, and cost breakdown.
24:35 Luca Moretti: Yep, we'll provision the creds and share by 2027-06-18.
24:52 Jordan Li: Anything else?
25:05 Priya Desai: Please send SOC2 summary and a template for KMS key policy.
25:18 Jordan Li: Noted — we'll send under NDA.
25:30 Amira Khan: Sounds good.
25:40 Jordan Li: Alright team — that's everything from our side. We'll follow up with the checklist, benchmark sheet, and the sample Helm chart.
25:55 Owen Park: Thanks all.
26:10 Meeting end.
